S:\;x^{2}+y^{2}+2gx+2fy+c=0\qquad(\text{centre }C(-g,-f),\;R^{2}=g^{2}+f^{2}-c)
\]

and let \(AB\) be a chord of \(S\) which subtends a right angle at the origin \(O(0,0)\).
Denote by \(H(h,k)\) the foot of the perpendicular from \(O\) to the line \(AB\).

---

### 1.  Equation of the chord through \(H\)

Since \(OH\perp AB\), the line \(AB\) has normal vector \((h,k)\) and passes through
\(H\); therefore  

\[
AB:\; hx+ky=h^{2}+k^{2}\tag{1}
\]

---

### 2.  Intersection of (1) with the circle

Write a point of the line (1) as  

\[
(x,y)=(h,k)+\lambda (-k,h),\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R .
\]

Substituting this in the equation of \(S\) gives  

\[
\bigl(h^{2}+k^{2}\bigr)\lambda^{2}
+2\bigl(-gk+fh\bigr)\lambda
+\bigl(h^{2}+k^{2}+2(gh+fk)+c\bigr)=0. \tag{2}
\]

Let the two solutions of (2) be \(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}\); the corresponding
points are  

\[
A:\;(h-k\lambda_{1},\,k+h\lambda_{1}),\qquad 
B:\;(h-k\lambda_{2},\,k+h\lambda_{2}).
\]

---

### 3.  Condition for a right‑angle at the origin

\[
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}
&=(h-k\lambda_{1})(h-k\lambda_{2})+(k+h\lambda_{1})(k+h\lambda_{2})\\
&=(h^{2}+k^{2})\bigl(1+\lambda_{1}\lambda_{2}\bigr).     \tag{3}
\end{aligned}
\]

The chord subtends a right angle at \(O\) iff \(\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}=0\);
since \(h^{2}+k^{2}\neq0\) (otherwise the line would be undefined), (3) yields  

\[
\lambda_{1}\lambda_{2}=-1.\tag{4}
\]

From (2) the product of the roots is  

\[
\lambda_{1}\lambda_{2}
=\frac{h^{2}+k^{2}+2(gh+fk)+c}{h^{2}+k^{2}}.\tag{5}
\]

Equating (4) and (5) we obtain  

\[
h^{2}+k^{2}+2(gh+fk)+c=-\bigl(h^{2}+k^{2}\bigr) .
\]

Hence  

\[
2\bigl(h^{2}+k^{2}\bigr)+2(gh+fk)+c=0,
\]

or, after dividing by 2,

\[
\boxed{x^{2}+y^{2}+gx+fy+\frac{c}{2}=0},\qquad (x,y)=(h,k).
\]

---

### 4.  Geometric description

The locus is a circle with centre  

\[
\left(-\frac{g}{2},-\frac{f}{2}\right)
\]

and radius  

\[
\rho=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{g^{2}+f^{2}-2c}.
\]

It is real (i.e. such chords actually exist) precisely when  

\[
|OC|^{2}=g^{2}+f^{2}\le 2R^{2},
\]

i.e. the distance from the origin to the centre of the given circle does not exceed
\(\sqrt{2}\) times its radius.

Thus the required locus of the feet of the perpendiculars from the origin to all
chords of \(S\) that subtend a right angle at the origin is the circle  

\[
\boxed{x^{2}+y^{2}+gx+fy+\dfrac{c}{2}=0}.
\]   (the origin itself is excluded when it satisfies the equation).<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
